title: Instruments built from polyhedra play the folk tune Sakura Sakura in a landscape of polyhedra
summary: On Tue 17 Nov at 15:59Z @yonderdavid.bsky.social (971 followers) posted a video with no text. Its alt text reads: "Animated instruments composed of polyhedra play the Japanese folk tune さくら さくら while the camera explores a landscape composed of regular polyhedra. The landscape features many sakura trees." It has 61 likes, 5 reposts, 7 replies and 7 quotes. The day before, @oscillatory.net (274 followers) had posted "it's polyhedra week"; one minute after the video the maker replied in that thread, quoting the video: "Perfect, I had about three hundred thousand mostly regular polyhedra lying around and needed something to do with them." @norvid-studies.bsky.social quote-posted the video with "it's polyhedra week now, lock in" (42 likes). Asked whether the koto sound was an existing physical model, the maker replied "New. Second draft, mostly vibed.", shared the code ("Koto information wants to be free."), and explained: "My first thought was just that I wanted to hear polyhedra, so that gave rise to the glass chimes and bell and drums." Between 20:53Z and 21:20Z the maker posted an eight-post account of how the video was made: it is generated in Blender, with Claude turning descriptions into Python and stills for the maker to judge; the first request was "Moebius but it's all polyhedra," and the scene description was just the song name; a series of change requests followed (pile the polyhedra, give every polyhedron collision, make the pavilion's legs a stack of polyhedra, remove the "mortar" look); it ends "Oh, and I had to tell it to make the river move." The video set off several other things made the same day and the next (see made-polyhedral-coffee-simulator, made-mobius-chess-ringmate, made-polykatamari).

made.what: video: instruments made of polyhedra (koto, glass chimes, bell, drums are named in the maker's posts) play a folk tune in a landscape of polyhedra

couldBeShown: Instruments assembled from regular polyhedra playing a tune; a camera moving through a landscape of piled polyhedra with trees, water, a bridge, a pavilion on stacked legs, a temple bell and a koto stage (all named in the maker's process posts); the successive drafts, which the maker posted as stills with short alt texts ("A first draft of the sakura landscape.", "Giving the polyhedra collision.", "First improvement."). Colours and the exact look are not described in the data, though another member says they borrowed the video's colour scheme. The studio draws in lines, and the maker's first change request says "Not every single outline would have to be rendered clearly to make the effect work ... just most of the edges."
